content: Polyethylene glycol-electrolyte solution (PEG-ES) is a medication prescribed to cleanse the bowel prior to gastrointestinal examinations or surgical procedures. It achieves this effect by inducing diarrhea. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. PEG-ES is provided as a powder that must be prepared into a solution for oral consumption. The solution should be prepared in the container provided, following the instructions on the label meticulously. Once prepared, an 8-ounce glass of the solution should be consumed rapidly every 10 minutes until the prescribed volume has been ingested or until your stool becomes watery, clear, and free of solid matter. Your doctor will specify the time at which you should begin drinking the solution. It is important to refrain from eating for at least 3 to 4 hours before starting PEG-ES. Additionally, you should avoid taking any oral medications within one hour of starting PEG-ES. Bowel movements typically begin within one hour of starting the solution. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take PEG-ES exactly as directed, without altering the dosage or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. Before taking PEG-ES, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to PEG-ES or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins and herbal supplements. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had any gastrointestinal diseases or obstructions. Additionally, inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. PEG-ES may cause side effects. Mild side effects include upset stomach, stomach pain, bloating, vomiting, and rectal irritation. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects, such as rash, hives, or skin irritation, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. The mixed solution should be stored in the refrigerator and used within 48 hours. Discard any medication that is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal instructions. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
